## What it is

- The **5F6-A** came in **1958**, the last of the tweed Bassmans; the 5F6 (1957) introduced the three-knob tone stack (Wikipedia, "Fender Bassman").
- Two 6L6 valves, a **GZ34 valve rectifier**, four 10" Jensen speakers in an open-back combo (Wikipedia).
- Made for bass, it became a rock and roll guitar amp (Buddy Holly), and Marshall copied it for the JTM45 (Wikipedia).

## How it makes its sound

- Its tone stack is the one Yeh and Smith worked out exactly: 250 pF, 20 nF, 20 nF, a 56 kΩ resistor and the three pots. The **tone stack** (Treble, Middle, Bass) is a passive network of three capacitors and resistors: it can only cut. This page computes its curve exactly from the component values, with the formula Yeh and Smith published in 2006 (checked there against a circuit simulator); the graph under the panel shows it.
- A **valve rectifier** cannot deliver current fast: when you hit a loud chord the supply droops (**sag**) and the amp compresses, then recovers.
- Two channels (Bright and Normal), jumpered here like the Marshall; Presence after the power amp.

## The amp

The Fender Bassman 5F6-A's control panel, drawn after photos (positions approximate, no logos). Drag a knob (or use the arrow keys), click a switch, then press a ▶ button. The guitar is this site's pickup model; **Pedals in front** puts one of the site's pedal models before the amp. Nobody has compared the sound with a real amp. ## Guided tour

```{=html}
<div class="amp-step" data-amp="bassman" data-set="{&quot;vol1&quot;:3,&quot;vol2&quot;:2}" data-play="chord"><p><b>Low volumes.</b> Warm clean.</p></div>
<div class="amp-step" data-amp="bassman" data-set="{&quot;vol1&quot;:6,&quot;vol2&quot;:4}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Volumes 6 / 4.</b> Edge of break-up.</p></div>
<div class="amp-step" data-amp="bassman" data-set="{&quot;vol1&quot;:9,&quot;vol2&quot;:7}" data-play="chord"><p><b>Up high.</b> Listen for the sag on the chord's attack.</p></div>
<div class="amp-step" data-amp="bassman" data-set="{&quot;vol1&quot;:5,&quot;vol2&quot;:3,&quot;middle&quot;:0}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Middle 0.</b> The deepest scoop of the stack.</p></div>
<div class="amp-step" data-amp="bassman" data-set="{&quot;vol1&quot;:5,&quot;vol2&quot;:3,&quot;middle&quot;:10,&quot;treble&quot;:3}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Middle 10, Treble 3.</b> Fat and dark.</p></div>
```

## Works Cited

<!-- works-cited: written by scripts/works-cited.py -->
::: {.works-cited}
"Fender Bassman." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fender_Bassman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fender_Bassman). 5F6 1957 three-knob tone stack, long-tailed-pair phase inverter; 5F6-A 1958 GZ34 rectifier, Presence change; four 10" Jensen P10R; copied by the Marshall JTM45; Buddy Holly.

"Tone stack." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tone_stack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tone_stack). The Bassman 5F6-A standardised the three-knob tone stack; passive, it can only cut; links the Tone Stack Calculator (TSC).

Yeh, David T., and Julius O. Smith. "Discretization of the '59 Fender Bassman Tone Stack." *Proceedings of the 9th International Conference on Digital Audio Effects (DAFx-06)*, Montreal, 2006. [ccrma.stanford.edu/~dtyeh/papers/yeh06_dafx.pdf](https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~dtyeh/papers/yeh06_dafx.pdf). Eqn. 1: the closed-form transfer function in the Treble / Middle / Bass pot positions, checked against SPICE in the paper; bilinear discretisation (2.3); Bassman values C1 250 pF, C2 = C3 20 nF, R1 250k, R2 1M, R3 25k, R4 56k.
:::
